author: DTrim99
body:
Agreed on both counts — the single-year proxy is the only thing either engine can do (PolicyEngine also only sees the 2021 record, so the 2020/2019 fallback tests are unmodelable for us too), and PolicyEngine's gate is checking the wrong quantity.

SB 1734 defines the test precisely (Laws 2023, ch. 147, §3.N.4): "'Tax liability' means the taxpayer's taxable income multiplied by the taxpayer's applicable tax rate... minus the sum of **nonrefundable and refundable** income tax credits claimed by the taxpayer under title 43, chapter 10, article 5" — which matches the DOR FAQ you quoted (credits reducing tax to zero → ineligible). PolicyEngine currently gates on tax *before* credits (26.53 ≥ 1 → passes), but the statutory liability here is 26.53 − 100 dependent credit − 80 family income tax credit − 50 excise credit < $1, so this record fails the 2021 test and should get no rebate. TAXSIM's refusal is correct.

Everything else reconciles exactly: both engines and the TaxAct return agree at −$50 for 2021 (tax 27 wiped by the dependent and family income tax credits, plus the $50 refundable increased excise credit). Filed PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9098; the fix gates the rebate on after-credit liability, which brings PolicyEngine to −50 with no srebate for this record.

Example household:
```
taxsimid,year,state,mstat,page,sage,depx,pwages,rentpaid,idtl
6714703,2021,3,1,25,0,1,19824.225,9793.8545,5
```
